subject.title: [Bug P2] scheduleReconnect() has no max retry limit — infinite reconnect loop

question: Should GatewayClient gain an opt-in reconnect-attempt cap, and which short-lived callers should opt into it while node-host remains unlimited by default?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the default retry policy is a product/compatibility choice because long-lived node-host recovery relies on unbounded reconnects.

options.title: Repair opt-in package cap
options.body: Add the cap in packages/gateway-client, keep the default unlimited, wire only approved short-lived callers, and require proof for both capped and uncapped behavior.

options.title: Keep unlimited reconnects
options.body: Reject a retry cap for now and close the linked PR after documenting why reconnect supervision belongs outside GatewayClient.

options.title: Defer to replacement PR
options.body: Close the stale conflicting candidate and ask for a fresh PR against the package client with maintainer-approved caller policy.

recommendation.title: Repair opt-in package cap
recommendation.body: Add the cap in packages/gateway-client, keep the default unlimited, wire only approved short-lived callers, and require proof for both capped and uncapped behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: History ties this gateway control-plane behavior and package extraction to steipete, and the decision is about the core GatewayClient contract.
